Ана эй ҷӯраи ҷон, биё ба хона биравем,
Пули билет бигирем, ба Расия биравем.
Мо ҳам пул кор бикунем, билети ҳарбӣ бихарем,
То ки аз хизмати ҳарбӣ, мо ҳам озод шавем.
examples.ref: 2009, Манучеҳр Миршариф [Manučehr Miršarif], “Аблава [Ablava, Impressment]”:
examples.english:
Come on dear friend, let’s go home,
Let’s buy a ticket and go to Russia.
We’ll earn some money too, and buy a military ID,
So that we also can be freed from military service.

examples.text: Аз бозе ки вақоиъро таърих қайд мекунад, то имрӯз дар диёри Мовароуннаҳру Туркистон чунон ки як қавми муаззам ба номи тоҷик ё ки тозик истиқомат дорад, ҳамчунон забону адабиёти эшон ҳам ривоҷ ёфта омадааст.
examples.ref: 1926, Sadriddin Ayni, Намунаи адабиёти тоҷик [An Anthology of Tajik Literature], Moscow: Чопхонаи миллиятҳои Шарқи ИҶШС [Printing House of the Nationalities of the East of the USSR], page 7:
examples.english: Just as there has been a great nation known as the Tajiks or Taziks in the lands of Transoxiana and Turkestan from the time that historical events began to be recorded up to today, so too their language and literature have continued to flourish.
examples.roman: Az boze ki vaqoyi'ro ta'rix qayd mekunad, to imrüz dar diyor-i Movarounnahru Turkiston čunon ki yak qavm-i muazzam ba nom-i tojik yo ki tozik istiqomat dorad, hamčunon zabonu adabiyot-i ešon ham rivoj yofta omadaast.
examples.translation: Just as there has been a great nation known as the Tajiks or Taziks in the lands of Transoxiana and Turkestan from the time that historical events began to be recorded up to today, so too their language and literature have continued to flourish.

Inherited from Classical Persian شَاهْمَاتْ (šāh-māt, “checkmate”, literally “the king is stunned”). By surface analysis, шоҳ (šoh, “king”) + мот (mot, “stunned, amazed”). The usage of it to mean "chess" is a phono-semantic matching of Russian шахматы (šaxmaty, “chess”). Compare Azerbaijani şahmat (“chess”).

etymology_text:
Inherited from Classical Persian رَحْمَت (rahmat, “mercy, compassion, commiseration”), from Arabic رَحْمَة (raḥma).
Interjection sense 1 may be a semantic loan from French merci (“thanks”, literally “mercy”), whence Russian мерси (mersi, “thanks”), and is widespread in usage across post-Soviet Central Asia. Compare Uzbek rahmat, Kazakh рахмет (raxmet), рақмет (raqmet), Kyrgyz ыракмат (ırakmat), Bashkir рәхмәт (räxmät), Tatar рәхмәт (räxmät), Uyghur رەھمەت (rehmet).

etymology_templates.name: ety

args.3: uz:kimGernot Windfuhr, John R. Perry (2009), “Persian and Tajik” (chapter 8), in The Iranian Languages (in English), page 440: Assimilated into the Tajik literary language is a series of Uzbek-Tajik hybrids formed from Uzbek kim 'who?': kim-kī 'someone (or other), anyone', kim-čī 'something, anything', kim-kadom 'some-N or other': vay az kim-čī no-rozī ast 'she's unhappy about something,' kim-kadom vaqt 'sometime or other, whenever', dar kim-kujo-ho 'somewhere or other'. As opposed to the Persian series kas-i/kas-e, jā'i/jo-e, čiz-i/čiz-e, etc., the kim series is unambiguously non-specific indefinite. >>

etymology_text: By surface analysis, вазн (vazn, “weight”) + -ин (-in, adjective-forming suffix), but etymologically likely inherited from Classical Persian وَزِین (wazīn), from Arabic وَزِين (wazīn), from the root و ز ن (w z n) related to weighing. Note that it is commonplace in Transoxanian Persian for an /n/ to unetymologically appear in words that did not have one in Classical Persian, though it typically intrudes either word-finally or before /g/.

examples.text: Мусобиқаи мазкур бо ибтикории Ассамблеяи байналхалқии “Дӯстии миллатҳо” дар ҳамкории бо Клубии варзишии Ҷоизадори Бозиҳои Олимпии Пекин-2008 Расул Боқиев “New Fitness”, Кумитаи кор бо ҷавонон ва варзиши Шурои ҷамъиятии назди Сафорати Ҷумҳурии Тоҷикистон дар Федератсияи Русия бо дастгирии Федератсияи ҷудои Тоҷикистон баргузор мегардад.
examples.ref: 2026 April 18, “Дар шаҳри Москва Чемпионати кушод оид ба ҷудо таҳти унвони “Дӯстии халқҳо” оғоз гардид”, in Khovar.tj:
examples.english: The aforementioned competition is being held at the initiative of The International Assembly "Friendship of Nations" in cooperation with the sports club of the 2008 Bejing Olympic Games Winner Rasul Baqiyev "New Fitness", The Committee is working with the Council of Youths and Sports by the Embassy of the Republic of Tajikistan in the Russian Federation with the support of the Tajikistan Judo Association.
examples.roman: Musobiqa-yi mazkur bo ibtikori-yi Assambleya-yi baynalxalqi-yi “Düsti-yi millatho” dar hamkori-yi bo Klubi-yi varziši-yi Joyizador-i Boziho-yi Olimpi-yi Pekin-2008 Rasul Boqiyev “New Fitness”, Kumita-yi kor bo javonon va varziš-i Šuro-yi jam'iyati-yi nazd-i Saforat-i Jumhuri-yi Tojikiston dar Federatsiya-yi Rusiya bo dastgiri-yi Federatsiya-yi judo-yi Tojikiston barguzor megardad.
examples.translation: The aforementioned competition is being held at the initiative of The International Assembly "Friendship of Nations" in cooperation with the sports club of the 2008 Bejing Olympic Games Winner Rasul Baqiyev "New Fitness", The Committee is working with the Council of Youths and Sports by the Embassy of the Republic of Tajikistan in the Russian Federation with the support of the Tajikistan Judo Association.

etymology_text:
Doublet of ҳаволӣ (havoli, “environs, outskirts”), from Classical Persian حَوَالِی (hawālī), from Arabic حَوَالَىٰ (ḥawālā). Compare Dari حَویلِی (hawēlī, “courtyard”), a form reshaped by imala, which becomes اَوْلِی (awlī) in colloquial Kabuli.
Though it has alternatively been suggested to derive from Ottoman Turkish آولی (avlı), a loanword from Greek, this explanation fails to account for the fact that it is pronounced with a voiceless pharyngeal fricative in the dialects of Tajik Persian that preserve it in borrowings from Arabic.
